title: HSK Standard Course 1
publisher: Beijing Language and Culture University Press
verifyNote: Word lists, glosses, grammar points and page numbers transcribed from the printed HSK Standard Course 1 (北京语言大学出版社). Over-syllabus words are flagged with "star": true. Sentences are authored from words already taught (checked by tools/check.mjs) and cover each lesson’s grammar points.

lessons.title: 你好！
lessons.topic: Greeting someone and asking how they are

grammar.title: Greetings are set phrases
grammar.pattern: 你好 / 您好 / 你们好
grammar.tip: 好 after a pronoun makes a fixed greeting with no verb: 你好 to one person, 您好 to someone you respect, 你们好 to a group. Nothing changes for the time of day.

grammar.title: Apologizing: 对不起 and 没关系
grammar.tip: 对不起 ("sorry") has an expected reply: 没关系 ("it's OK"). They travel together as a courtesy pair.

grammar.title: Thanking: 谢谢 and 不客气
grammar.tip: 谢谢 ("thanks") is answered with 不客气 ("you're welcome"). You can name the person thanked: 谢谢你, 谢谢你们.

grammar.title: Saying no with 不
grammar.tip: 不 negates what follows: 不客气 (not polite → you're welcome), 不好 (not good). It is the everyday "not".

lessons.title: 你叫什么名字？
lessons.topic: Names, and saying who someone is

grammar.title: The question word 什么
grammar.tip: 什么 means "what" and stands exactly where the answer goes, so the word order stays the same: 你叫什么名字？→ 我叫李月。

grammar.title: The 是 sentence: A is B
grammar.tip: 是 links two nouns, like "is/are": 我是学生 (I am a student). Negate it with 不是: 我不是老师.

grammar.title: Yes-no questions with 吗
grammar.tip: Add 吗 to the end of a statement to make a yes-no question, with no change in word order: 你是老师吗？ (are you a teacher?).

lessons.title: 她是我的汉语老师
lessons.titlePinyin: Tā shì wǒ de Hànyǔ lǎoshī

grammar.title: Asking "who" and "which" with 谁 and 哪
grammar.pattern: Subject + 是 + 谁 · 哪 + 国
grammar.tip: 谁 asks which person ("who"); 哪 asks which one out of a set. Both sit exactly where the answer will go, so the word order does not change between question and answer: 她是谁？→ 她是我的老师。

grammar.title: The possessive particle 的
grammar.tip: 的 links an owner to what they own, like English 's or "of": 我的老师 (my teacher), 他的朋友 (his friend). The owner comes first, then 的, then the thing.

grammar.title: The follow-up particle 呢 (1)
grammar.tip: 呢 turns a noun into a short "and how about …?" question that reuses the question already on the table. 我很好，你呢？ means "I'm fine, and you?" — no need to repeat the whole sentence.

sentences.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de Hànyǔ lǎoshī.
Tā shì nǐ de tóngxué ma?
Tā shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.
Nǐ péngyou shì nǎ guó rén?
sentences.en: What country is your friend from?

lessons.title: 她女儿今年二十岁
lessons.titleEn: Her daughter is twenty this year

grammar.title: Asking a small number with 几
grammar.tip: 几 asks "how many" when the answer is expected to be small (roughly under ten), and it always needs a measure word after it: 几岁 (how old), 几口人 (how many people in the family).

grammar.title: Numbers up to 100
grammar.tip: Chinese numbers stack simply: 二十 (20) is "two-ten", 二十一 (21) is "two-ten-one". Once you know 一 to 十, you can say every number up to 九十九.

grammar.title: 了 marking a change
grammar.tip: Sentence-final 了 says a new state has arrived. 她今年二十岁了 means she has now turned twenty — the 了 marks the change into that age.

grammar.title: Asking age with 多大
grammar.tip: 多 + an adjective asks "how ___?". 多大 literally "how big" is the ordinary way to ask an adult's age: 你多大？ For a small child you ask 几岁 instead.

grammar.title: Saying family size with 有
grammar.pattern: Subject + 家 + 有 + number + 口人
grammar.tip: To say how many people are in a family, use 家有 …口人: 我家有三口人 (there are three people in my family).

sentences.pinyin: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén?
sentences.en: How many people are in your family?

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu sān kǒu rén.
sentences.en: There are three people in my family.
How old is your daughter this year?
How old are you this year?
My daughter is three this year.

lessons.title: 我会说汉语
lessons.topic: Skills and how you do something

grammar.title: The modal verb 会 (1): a learned skill
grammar.tip: 会 before a verb means you can do something because you learned it: 我会说汉语 (I can speak Chinese), 她会做菜 (she can cook). It is about acquired skill, not permission.

grammar.title: Adjective predicates with 很
grammar.tip: An adjective can be the whole predicate with no 是: 菜很好吃 (the food is delicious). 很 usually fills the slot even when you do not mean "very" strongly — a bare adjective sounds like a comparison.

grammar.title: The question word 怎么 (1): how to do something
grammar.tip: 怎么 before a verb asks the manner or method: 这个字怎么读？ (how do you read this character?), 怎么写？ (how do you write it?).

sentences.pinyin: Māma zuò de cài hěn hǎochī.
sentences.en: The food mom makes is delicious.
How do you read the character?
How do you write Chinese characters?

sentences.pinyin: Nǐ māma huì shuō Hànyǔ ma?
Lǎoshī shuō de zì hěn hǎo.
sentences.en: The characters the teacher reads out are good.

lessons.title: 今天几号？
lessons.topic: Dates, days of the week and going places

words.gloss: to look at; to read; to watch

grammar.title: Saying a date (1): month and day
grammar.tip: A date is built big-to-small: the month, then the day. 五月三号 is "May 3rd" (literally five-month three-day). The day of the week 星期 works the same way: 星期一 is Monday.

grammar.title: Nominal predicates for dates and age
grammar.tip: For dates, days and ages you can drop 是 and let the noun be the predicate: 今天三号 (today is the 3rd), 她二十岁 (she is twenty). 是 comes back when the sentence is negated with 不.

grammar.title: Serial verbs (1): going somewhere to do something
grammar.tip: Two verbs can share one subject in order of what happens: 去 + place first, then what you do there. 我去学校看书 = I go to school (and there) read.

sentences.en: I am going to school tomorrow.
I go to school to read.
Excuse me, what is the date today?

sentences.pinyin: Nǐ míngtiān qù kàn shū ma?
sentences.en: Are you going to read tomorrow?

grammar.title: The modal verb 想: wanting to do something
grammar.tip: 想 before a verb means "would like to": 我想喝茶 (I'd like to drink tea), 我想买杯子 (I want to buy a cup). On its own 想 can also mean "to miss (someone)".

grammar.title: The question word 多少
grammar.tip: 多少 asks "how many/how much" for any amount, large or small, and needs no measure word: 多少钱？ (how much money?). Use it, not 几, once the answer might be a big number.

grammar.title: The measure words 个 and 口
grammar.tip: A number cannot sit straight before a noun; a measure word goes between. 个 is the all-purpose one (三个杯子, three cups); 口 is used for counting family members (三口人).

grammar.title: Saying an amount of money
grammar.tip: 块 is the spoken word for the yuan: 三块 or 三块钱 both mean "three yuan". You may add 钱 at the end or leave it off.

sentences.en: Would you like to eat rice?

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ xiàwǔ qù shāngdiàn mǎi chá.
sentences.en: I go to the shop to buy tea in the afternoon.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí ge bēizi.
sentences.en: I want to buy a cup.

grammar.title: The verb 在: being somewhere
grammar.tip: As a main verb 在 says where something is: 猫在椅子下面 (the cat is under the chair). The place comes straight after 在, with no extra "is".

grammar.title: The question word 哪儿
grammar.tip: 哪儿 asks "where" and stands in the place slot: 你儿子在哪儿工作？ The answer drops into the same spot: 他在医院工作。

grammar.title: The preposition 在: where an action happens
grammar.tip: Before another verb, 在 + place tells where the action happens: 他在医院工作 (he works at the hospital). The 在-phrase comes before the verb, never after it.

grammar.title: The follow-up particle 呢 (2): asking where
grammar.tip: 呢 after a noun can ask "where is …?" when location is what everyone is already talking about: 我的书呢？ means "Where is my book?".

sentences.en: The cat is under the chair.
My dad works at the hospital.

sentences.pinyin: Bàba de gǒu zài yǐzi xiàmian.
sentences.en: Dad's dog is under the chair.

words.gloss: to not have; there is not

grammar.title: The 有 sentence: something exists somewhere
grammar.tip: 有 says something is present at a place: 桌子上有电脑 (there is a computer on the table). The place comes first, then 有, then what is there.

grammar.title: The conjunction 和: joining nouns
grammar.tip: 和 links two nouns, like "and": 我和朋友 (my friend and I), 茶和水 (tea and water). It joins things, not whole sentences or verbs.

grammar.title: The modal verb 能: being able / allowed
grammar.tip: 能 before a verb means able or allowed to, often about the situation right now: 我能坐这儿吗？ (can I sit here?). 会 is for learned skills; 能 is for possibility and permission.

grammar.title: Polite requests with 请
grammar.tip: 请 before a verb makes a polite request: 请坐 (please sit), 请问 (may I ask). It softens an order into an invitation.

sentences.en: There is a computer on the desk.

sentences.pinyin: Yǐzi shàng yǒu yì běn shū.
sentences.en: There is a book on the chair.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ hé Wáng Fāng shì tóngxué.
sentences.en: Wang Fang and I are classmates.
The computer is on the desk.

sentences.pinyin: Xiè Péng de diànnǎo zài nǎr?

sentences.en: There is a chair behind the desk.

grammar.title: Telling clock time
grammar.tip: Clock time reads hour then minute: 两点十分 is 2:10 (two-o'clock ten-minutes). Note the hour "two" is 两, not 二, before 点.

grammar.title: Time words come before the verb
grammar.tip: A when-word sits between the subject and the verb, never after it: 我现在回家 (I'm going home now), 我们中午吃饭 (we eat at noon).

grammar.title: The noun 前: "before"
grammar.tip: 前 after a time span means "ago / before": 三天前 (three days ago). It follows the amount of time rather than coming in front of it.

sentences.en: We go to see a movie at noon.
We are going to eat now.

grammar.title: The question word 怎么样
grammar.tip: 怎么样 asks "how is it? / how about it?": 明天天气怎么样？ (what's the weather like tomorrow?). It stands where a description would go.

grammar.title: A subject-predicate phrase as predicate
grammar.tip: A sentence can describe a topic by giving a small subject-plus-comment about part of it: 他身体很好 (as for him, his health is good). The whole "身体很好" describes 他.

grammar.title: The adverb 太 … 了: too much
grammar.tip: 太 before an adjective, usually closed with 了, means "too / excessively": 太热了 (it's too hot). The 了 is part of the fixed frame here.

grammar.title: The modal verb 会 (2): likely to happen
grammar.tip: 会 can also mean something is likely: 明天会下雨 (it will probably rain tomorrow). This is a prediction, different from 会 meaning a learned skill.

sentences.en: What will the weather be like tomorrow?
I want to drink some water.

sentences.pinyin: Xiǎojiě, nǐ xiǎng chī xiē shuǐguǒ ma?
sentences.en: Miss, would you like some fruit?

sentences.pinyin: Tiānqì tài rè le, wǒ xiǎng hē shuǐ.
sentences.en: The weather is too hot; I want to drink water.

lessons.title: 他在学做中国菜呢
lessons.titlePinyin: Tā zài xué zuò Zhōngguó cài ne
lessons.titleEn: He's learning to cook Chinese food

grammar.title: The interjection 喂
grammar.tip: 喂 is the standard way to open a phone call, like "hello?": 喂，你好！ It is used to get attention, not as a greeting you'd write.

grammar.title: Action in progress with 在 … 呢
grammar.tip: 在 before the verb (often closed with 呢) says the action is happening right now: 他在学做菜呢 (he is learning to cook). It marks ongoing action, like English "-ing".

grammar.title: Reading out a phone number
grammar.tip: Phone numbers are read one digit at a time. In this context 1 is spoken yāo instead of yī, to keep it clear over the phone.

grammar.title: The particle 吧: softening a suggestion
grammar.tip: 吧 at the end turns a statement into a gentle suggestion or guess: 我们去吧 (let's go), 你是老师吧？ (you're a teacher, right?).

sentences.pinyin: Tā zài xuéxí zuò cài ne.

sentences.en: Let's go make a phone call.

sentences.pinyin: Nǐ yě xǐhuan kàn diànyǐng ma?
sentences.en: Do you also like watching movies?

lessons.title: 她买了不少衣服
lessons.titlePinyin: Tā mǎi le bù shǎo yīfu
lessons.titleEn: She bought quite a lot of clothes

words.gloss: to see; to catch sight of

grammar.title: 了 marking a completed action
grammar.tip: After a verb, 了 says the action happened or is finished: 她买了不少衣服 (she bought quite a few clothes). This is completion, distinct from the "change" 了 at the end of a sentence.

grammar.title: The noun 后: "after"
grammar.tip: 后 follows a time span or event to mean "after": 五分钟后 (after five minutes), 下课后 (after class). It comes at the end, unlike English "after".

grammar.title: The particle 啊: warmth and emphasis
grammar.tip: 啊 at the end adds a friendly, exclamatory tone: 真漂亮啊！ (how pretty!). It softens and warms the sentence rather than changing its meaning.

grammar.title: The adverb 都: "all / both"
grammar.tip: 都 sits before the verb and sums up everything mentioned before it: 这些衣服都很漂亮 (these clothes are all pretty). It looks back at the plural subject.

sentences.pinyin: Tā mǎi le bù shǎo yīfu.
sentences.en: She has bought quite a few clothes.

sentences.zh: 我看见先生开车回来了。
sentences.pinyin: Wǒ kànjiàn xiānsheng kāichē huílai le.
sentences.en: I saw the gentleman drive back.
He will be back in five minutes.

sentences.pinyin: Zhèxiē dōngxi dōu shì wǒ de.

sentences.en: Sir, how much are these apples?

lessons.title: 我是坐飞机来的
lessons.titlePinyin: Wǒ shì zuò fēijī lái de
lessons.topic: Travel, and emphasising details with 是…的

grammar.title: The 是 … 的 structure: highlighting how/when/where
grammar.tip: 是 … 的 frames the part of a past event you want to stress — when, where or how it happened: 我是坐飞机来的 (it was by plane that I came). The verb sits inside the frame.

grammar.title: Saying a full date (2): year, month, day
grammar.pattern: number + 年 + number + 月 + number + 号
grammar.tip: A full date runs biggest to smallest: year, then month, then day. 二〇一三年五月三号 is "May 3rd, 2013". The year is read digit by digit.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ shì zuò fēijī lái de.

sentences.en: I am glad to meet you.

sentences.pinyin: Tā shì zuò chūzūchē lái de.

sentences.zh: 我们一起去饭店吃饭吧。
sentences.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ qù fàndiàn chīfàn ba.
sentences.en: Let's go eat at the restaurant together.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan tīng lǎoshī shuō Hànyǔ.
sentences.en: I like listening to the teacher speak Chinese.

sentences.pinyin: Nǐ shì nǎ nián lái de?

sentences.en: I am very glad to know you.
